claims: California Assembly Bill 2624 (AB 2624) is nicknamed the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" by critics.
AB 2624 is sponsored by Assemblymember Mia Bonta.
AB 2624 is officially titled "Privacy for immigration support services providers".
AB 2624 proposes enhancing confidentiality for employees and volunteers.
AB 2624 proposes limiting the release of home/work addresses of employees and volunteers.
As of mid-April 2026, AB 2624 has passed its early stages.
As of mid-April 2026, AB 2624 sits in the California Assembly Judiciary Committee.
Critics including Assemblymember Carl DeMaio argue AB 2624 shields fraudulent organizations from citizen journalists such as Nick Shirley.
Nick Shirley exposes fraud via viral videos.
Critics allege AB 2624 is designed to stop independent investigations into taxpayer-funded organizations.
Critics allege AB 2624 specifically targets videos posted by online influencers like Nick Shirley.
Supporters (Democrats) argue AB 2624 protects workers from targeted harassment and violence in a tense political climate.
Opponents (Republicans) argue AB 2624 is an unconstitutional violation of the First Amendment that "criminalizes" journalism.
